get.description:
Verifies the attempt and Google's ID token, then signs in (session cookie) and
redirects to ``next``. Any failure redirects to ``/login?error=<code>`` with a stable
code (``google_state_invalid``, ``google_cancelled``, ``google_failed``,
``email_not_allowed``, ``consent_required``, ...); details go to the audit log only.
get.summary: Google sends the browser back here

post.description:
Returns Google's sign-in URL and sets a short-lived httpOnly cookie that ties the
attempt to this browser. 404 ``google_signin_unavailable`` when Google is off.

get.description: Also re-issues the CSRF cookie, so a client that lost it can recover.

post.description:
Send a 6-digit code (valid 10 minutes) to the address.

The response is the same whether or not an account exists. Requesting a new code
invalidates any earlier unused one. Rate-limited per address and per IP (429).

Verify the code and start a session (cookie). Creates the account on first use,
which requires ``age_confirmed`` and ``accept_terms``; an account without a recorded age
confirmation needs ``age_confirmed`` too. Five wrong guesses lock a code.

Works both ways: no chat, no intros, no matches between you, and your connection
ends for good. They aren't told. Calling it again changes nothing. Unblocking later
does not reopen the connection.

get.description: Report that the process is up. Touches no dependencies, so it stays cheap.
Check PostgreSQL and the pgvector extension. Returns 503 if either fails.

post.description: The moderator sees a copy of the intro's request and note. The sender is not told.

Accepting connects you: you both see each other's name and links. Declining is
never shown to the sender.

The other person sees your request, the match reason and your note, but not your
name or links until they accept.
post.summary: Send an intro to a match

delete.description:
Schedule permanent deletion after the grace period (30 days by default).

Signs out every device immediately; signing in is refused during the grace period.

patch.description:
Name, links, timezone, languages and visibility (``paused`` hides the profile from
new matches). The about text changes only through ``PUT``.

put.description:
Saves at once. If the about text changed, ``parse_status`` is ``pending`` until a
background job has read it (usually seconds); poll ``GET /me/profile``.

503.description: Storage nearly full; try again later.

put.description:
Replaces the parsed summary, offers, seeks, interests and availability with the
user's version; matching uses it from the next embedding (a background job).
put.summary: Correct what was understood from my profile

get.description:
Start without `after` to get a cursor, then pass the returned `cursor` each time.

Poll on this cadence (ADR 0012): every 3 s for a minute after a message, every 10 s
until 5 quiet minutes, every 30 s until 10 quiet minutes, then stop until the person
is back; never while the app is hidden. If `poll_after_seconds` is set, wait that long.
get.summary: Poll for new messages in all your conversations

post.description:
Report a message the other person sent. The moderator sees a copy of it and the 10
messages before it. The other person is not told, and you won't hear what happens.

Signs them out everywhere at once. They can't sign in, can't be messaged and aren't
shown in matches until unsuspended. Logged in the audit log.

409.description: `cannot_suspend`: your own, a moderator's, or not active.

post.description: They can sign in again. Logged in the audit log.
